_comment: Confirmed false positives, fed back to the verifier as LABELLED negative
exemplars — the local stand-in for the moderator '✕' loop that production
The IMAGES are not committed. They are other people's photographs, and the
same rule applies as to tools/eval/golden_sources.json: the manifest is the
artefact, the pixels are fetched. Put the files in .tmp/negatives/ (already
gitignored); a missing file is skipped, never fatal.
Every entry has been checked BY EYE at native resolution. 'hallucinatedText'
is what the detector claimed to read, verbatim — naming the invented string
next to the image that does not contain it is the whole lesson, and
verifier.build_negative_exemplars puts it in the label.
highSignal marks a rejection that overturned a CONFIDENT detection. Those
sort first, because there are only four slots and the model's confident
mistakes teach more than its hesitant ones.

whyItIsNotStelz: A white slim can held in a mirror selfie. At native 3024x4032 the
wordmark reads SAVRY, mirrored, above three cross symbols — a layout
Stëlz does not use on any product line.
Why it fools the detector: mirrored text defeats OCR, the can silhouette
and the white-on-slim livery match the reference packshots, and the
prompt has just shown eight photographs of Stëlz. The model fills the
unreadable label in from the strongest prior available, which is exactly
the failure mode a negative exemplar exists to counter.
Not caught by the verifier either: it returned no_readable_brand, which
decide() correctly treats as 'I cannot tell' rather than 'it is absent',
so the first pass stood. Nothing in the stored fields separates this row
from a true positive — hence a human decision, recorded here.
